Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the left-opening parabola shown above. Express the answer in terms of the variable $y.$

$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola has its vertex at $O,$ and passes through the point $(-3,-1).$

The general equation of a left- or right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0)$ is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Substituting $x=-3$ and $y=-1$ into the equation above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)^{2} & =4p(-3) \\ 1 & =-12p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of our parabola is 

$$
{y}^{2}=-\frac{1}{3}x.
$$

Finally, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{3}x) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{6y}\end{aligned}
$$
